adr_title: Legacy canvas-YAML interop reconciled — the `view` authority row, one level too high and stamped on three files for every one it fits
decision_statement: The legacy canvas_yaml_interop shape IS the Standard's `view` authority row — for the canvases it actually describes. Canonical placement is metadata.frontmatter._reserved. THE MIGRATION IS NOT ONE RECIPE: a canvas is derived iff `source_yaml` is non-empty AND the file resolves, in which case it takes source_name + authority: view + production: generated; otherwise it is a primary artifact and takes NONE of the three. `authority`/`production` are machine-enforced as A-8 since v2.4.0, both optional, asymmetric. Propagation is OFFERED to Rosetta, never performed.
context: ⭐ START WITH §What this ADR says today — Amendment 3 added it because the decision had become distributed across an August body plus two amendment blocks, so ratifying meant reconstructing it from what was struck. It is a SUMMARY, not a replacement: the Decisions remain the authority. THREE AMENDMENTS, ALL 2026-09-16, each correcting the one before. A1: Decision 4 claimed canvas_std does not know the `authority` key — false since Gridline shipped A-8 on 2026-09-11; A1 added a blanket `production: generated` row because A-8 is asymmetric. A2: ⛔ that row was WRONG FOR THE MAJORITY. The corpus is two populations. Measured and re-derived three times: 258 canvases across 63 vaults — 194 PRIMARY (sourceless; no template_*.lattice.yaml exists anywhere, verified with find), 63 DERIVED (source resolves), 1 bare. ≈3:1 against the recipe. And `view` is wrong on the 194, not merely incomplete — Plumbline P1 already ruled that a standalone hand-authored primary artifact 'is not diagrammatic context at all', so omission is correct. A3 closes what A1 and A2 left: (a) ⛔ AN ACTIVE TRAP — the `source_yaml` row still said 'a real value must be supplied' for the three that have none. `source_name` is an INPUT TO THE PARTITION TEST, so an invented value resolves nothing but changes the test's answer, silently reclassifying a primary canvas as derived. Self-concealing, and worse than an empty field, because the empty field IS the evidence. (b) The '4/4 reach adna_native [OK]' evidence verified the UNPARTITIONED recipe, so Decision 3's 'verified' claim rested on the wrong transcript — RE-RUN rather than merely withdrawn, on scratch copies, one canvas from each population: both reach adna_native [OK] with degradation intact, and the primary form carries no source_name, no authority and no production. (c) The sentence 'the view contract has been declared for 6 months without ever being enforced' is the misread itself — the emptiness was not debt, it was the evidence — struck. (d) The title asserted the whole corpus is the view row; corrected. ⚠ WHAT ALREADY SHIPPED is unchanged: v8.11 fired the RELOCATION half onto 8 files. They read core [OK] and adna_native FAIL, but they declare no conformance_level so they validate at core and pass — nothing is broken today — and Rosetta scoped the release to '8 files… NOT the fleet'. They verified placement and byte-identity, which is exactly what we asked of them. The stale recipe is ours.

consequences_positive.value: The decision is now readable in ONE place (§What this ADR says today) rather than reconstructed from an August body plus three amendment blocks.
Decision 3's 'verified' claim is TRUE AGAIN, of the recipe actually recommended — re-run on scratch copies, both populations reaching adna_native [OK] with degradation intact.
The partition test is executable, and the trap that would have defeated it is closed: never invent a source_name, because it is an input to the test rather than a description of the file.
The core reconciliation is untouched and still independently confirmed by Rosetta: the legacy is the Standard's `view` row at the wrong path, not a competing system.
No canvas_std change. This ratifies a DESCRIPTION, not a validator; the firewall stays at diff 0.

consequences_negative.value: ⛔ Ratifying endorses REMOVING `authority: view` from ~194 fleet canvases that have carried it since 2026-02. A deletion of a false claim, not of information — but a visible change to files many vaults hold.
⚠ Nothing enforces the partition in code. A `view` canvas citing a source that does not exist still validates OK — verified, not assumed. The test is doctrine, not machinery.
The 8 files v8.11 shipped stay core-valid and adna_native-invalid until the field-shape half lands. A KNOWN state, not an unmeasured one.
An erratum is owed to Rosetta, and it is now a BIGGER one than 'add a production row' — it is 'partition before migrating'. That is a cost of signing late, and it is ours.

This ADR needed three amendments in one day. Its substance held throughout; its SCOPE was wrong twice. A fourth population is not impossible — the test is derivable, so re-run it before any fleet migration.

alternatives.title: Sign with Amendment 1 only (the blanket `production` row)
alternatives.rejected_because: it would bless a recipe that stamps `production: generated` onto 194 canvases generated from nothing, on top of an `authority: view` that is false of them. This is the option Amendment 2 exists to prevent — and it is the option that was on the table yesterday.

alternatives.title: Keep `authority: view` on the primary canvases and add `production: hand_authored`
alternatives.rejected_because: legal under A-8's asymmetry, and it avoids churn — but it preserves the original error, asserting an owner that does not exist. Ruled against: omission is Plumbline P1's answer for this population.

alternatives.title: Deprecate the interop spec and regenerate all canvases from source
alternatives.rejected_because: throws away a working mapping and hundreds of hand-checked files — and for the 194 primary ones there IS no source to regenerate from. That is the whole finding.

alternatives.title: Teach canvas_std to read metadata._reserved as a fallback
alternatives.rejected_because: a firewall change (LIP territory) that would legitimize two canonical paths forever and weaken A-2 for every future document.

recommendation.rationale: RATIFY AS AMENDED (×3). The substance — the legacy IS the Standard's `view` row, at the wrong path — was right in August, Rosetta confirmed it independently, and no amendment has touched it. What was wrong, twice, was SCOPE: one recipe applied to two populations. That is now partitioned, verified under the recipe actually recommended, and stated in one place. ⚠ If ratifying a document amended three times in a day is uncomfortable, DEFER is clean — nothing is failing in the meantime, and the 8 shipped files pass at their declared level.
key_factors: Core reconciliation independently confirmed by Rosetta and untouched by all three amendments.
Partition re-derived three times (258 / 194 / 63 / 1); the negative verified with find, not assumed.
Decision 3's 'verified' restored with a fresh transcript covering BOTH populations.
§What this ADR says today makes it signable without reconstructing from strikes.
No code, no schema, no A-8 behaviour change; firewall diff 0.
risks: ⛔ Wrong twice about scope in one day. A third population may exist; the partition test is derivable — re-run before any fleet migration rather than trusting these figures.
Nothing validates that a `view` canvas has a resolving source, so the partition depends on whoever runs it.
Signing does not repair the 8 shipped files — that needs the erratum to reach Rosetta first.
